adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss read-state link light-scheme value inverted from 30% to 70%, washing out light-theme reply/read-state links instead of only affecting dark themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`, a link color that was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` is changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This reverses the typical pattern used elsewhere in the diff (light theme gets the darker primary value, dark theme gets the lighter secondary value). As written, the light-scheme value becomes much lighter (70% vs 30%), plausibly washing out link text in the light theme while making the dark theme value darker than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss .custom-message-length light value inverted from 70% to 30%, diverging from its desktop twin and giving mobile light users near-black hint text

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss, .custom-message-length changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which inverts the light-theme value (70% → 30%) compared to the desktop equivalent in desktop/modal.scss (`dark-light-choose(...70%, ...30%)`). This is a concrete, diff-verifiable mismatch likely causing noticeably darker (near-black) hint text for light users on mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/topic-post.scss h3 light branch changed from 20% to 50%, diverging from desktop/topic-post.scss and making mobile onebox titles lighter and inconsistent

In the same PR, the corresponding desktop rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` keeps the 20% lightness (now wrapped in `dark-light-choose(...20%..., ...80%...)`). This single deviation in mobile appears to be an unintended regression/inconsistency introduced by the diff.

The finding about inconsistency between coldmap (scheme-aware) and heatmap (hardcoded) is therefore diff-grounded, but it’s a design/contrast consistency concern rather than a clear functional defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/compose.scss:~174 — enabled-state rule adjacent to the converted .wmd-input:disabled still uses color: darken($primary, 40%), leaving hardcoded primary-based color that renders invisible darkened text on dark themes in the mobile reply composer textarea

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the diff converts the disabled-state backgrounds to `dark-light-choose(...)`, but immediately after that block the enabled `.wmd-input` rule still sets `color: darken($primary, 40%);` (unchanged in this PR). Given the PR’s widespread goal of replacing primary-based `scale-color(...)` usages with dark/light-aware colors, this is a specific, diff-grounded inconsistency (incomplete dark-theme adaptation). The claim that it becomes “invisible” on dark themes is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

This is a concrete inversion of the lightness values between the two branches compared to the desktop sibling and the general pattern in the diff (lighter primary for the first arg, darker/lower-lightness secondary for the second arg). adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.css.scss:89 converts a.new-user to dark-light-choose(...), but the embed pipeline may not support it and embeds have no scheme-switching mechanism, making the change dead, wrong, or build-breaking

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` changing `a.new-user` to use `dark-light-choose(...)`. However, the claim that the “embed pipeline may not support it” or that embeds “have no scheme-switching mechanism” is not verifiable from this diff alone. Also, the same `dark-light-choose(...)` function is introduced broadly across many other SCSS files in the same PR, which suggests it is expected to be available in the normal Sass compilation context rather than being uniquely problematic for embeds (nothing in the diff indicates embed.scss is compiled differently).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration sweep only converts scale-color($primary, ...) rules literally, leaving peers like darken($primary, 40%) untouched, causing inconsistent conventions and remaining dark-theme legibility bugs

adjudication.rationale: The diff performs a broad sweep replacing many `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` usages with `dark-light-choose(...)`, but it does not update other color transformations in the same files. For example, `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss` still contains `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` unchanged. That supports the finding that the migration is limited to literal `scale-color($primary, ...)` cases and leaves peers like `darken(...)` untouched, creating inconsistent conventions; however, the claim that this definitively causes dark-theme legibility bugs is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 light-theme value silently changed from $lightness 30% to 70%, making light-theme usernames in narrow post-controls render ~40 lightness points brighter (unintended visual regression)

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss:102 light-theme value inverted instead of mirrored: .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%, while desktop/modal.scss:50 correctly keeps 70%/30%, causing divergent rendering between platforms

adjudication.rationale: In `desktop/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` is updated to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, preserving the intended 70% (light) / 30% (dark) pairing. But in `mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` is changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which swaps/inverts the lightness values compared to desktop and the prior mobile value (70%). This creates a real, diff-verifiable platform divergence and likely incorrect color selection for the light theme on mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/user.scss:522 (and mobile/user.scss:497) light-theme .name color changed from 30% to 50%, flattening the visual hierarchy between .name and .title that the old 30/50 pairing established

Assuming `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` uses the first argument for the light theme, this makes `.name` and `.title` the same lightness in light mode, which can reduce the intended visual hierarchy. This is a UI/visual design concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~100 hand-maintained dark-light-choose scale-color mirror pairs with no single source of truth; should be replaced with named color variables or a muted() mixin to structurally enforce the mirror invariant

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces many repeated, manually specified `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))` expressions across numerous SCSS files (e.g., `common/base/_topic-list.scss` `th`, `td`, `.topic-excerpt`; `common/base/header.scss` notifications; `desktop/topic-list.scss` multiple icons/links; etc.). This repetition does create a maintainability risk with no single source of truth for the intended mirrored light/dark values, so the suggestion to consolidate via named variables or a mixin is a specific, diff-grounded architecture concern rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .names a in desktop/topic-post.scss:291 changes the light slot lightness from 30% to 70%, making light-theme username links washed-out — a light-theme regression outside the PR's stated intent
